page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.2xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine hosted on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz, providing 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of shared L3 cache. Standard instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, SHA-NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, whereas AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent.

Memory capacity is configured at 32.0 GB, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local disk storage, requiring external cloud block storage for persistent or scratch space. Graphics processing is unaccelerated with zero GPUs installed, and the instance operates with a baseline network bandwidth profile of 2 Gbps.

In synthetic compute benchmarks, the instance demonstrates restrained performance capabilities. Single-core execution in stress-ng yielded a score of 756.09, placing it in the bottom 10% tier. Multi-core stress-ng tests reached 3045.4, settling in the bottom 25% bracket. The AMD EPYC architecture delivers stable dedicated core allocations for baseline concurrency, but the per-core instruction throughput is comparatively low compared to more modern or compute-focused architectures.

Given its hardware distribution and baseline performance metrics, the ecs.g6a.2xlarge serves as a cost-conscious, balanced platform for general-purpose computing. Suitable workloads include mid-tier web application servers, standard microservice clusters, background job processors, staging infrastructure, and internal enterprise tools that require balanced memory density without intensive mathematical computations or high local I/O throughput.
